_comment: Which tool calls a Workbench thread runs WITHOUT a permission card, for assistants whose assistant.json says "autoAllow": "readOnly" (assistants/PATTERNS.md §5; owner, 2026-10-16: designer threads should not ask before reading). Read by WorkbenchAutoAllow.swift. Read-only means: a read tool, a shell line made only of the commands below with no write redirect, the scripts below, or an applet verb whose kind is "read" in applet-verbs.json. Everything else asks, as before, and a missing or unreadable file auto-allows nothing. Writes keep their card, which has Allow All. DECODER SAFETY: comment keys at this TOP LEVEL ONLY.
_readOnlyCommandsWhy: Each only reads or prints. Left out on purpose: awk (system(), print > file), tee, xargs, env, sh/bash/zsh -c, python -c, uniq (a second file argument is an OUTPUT), curl, open.
_sedWhy: sed scripts can write (w) or execute (e), so only a line-range print is read-only: sed -n '1,80p' file.
_neverAutoAllowedVerbsWhy: Verbs applet-verbs.json calls "read" that can also write: openJingle with load: true installs parts onto the LoopStar board. A verb that writes in ANY mode is listed here or relabelled; WorkbenchAutoAllowTests fails on a write-sounding read verb that is neither.
_sensitiveWhy: A read of these still asks: secrets would otherwise reach the model without anyone seeing the request.
